summary: Reviewed AbstractLanguageRendererTest.php against all four review dimensions: maintainability, best practices, performance, and future context.
Identified one Blocking issue (temp file leak) and one Fix-Forward issue (assertNotFalse alignment); applied both directly.

Fix 1 (reviewer-applied-fix): Added $tempFiles tracking array and tearDown() method to unlink temp JSON files created by readerFromArray(). The sibling IconBuilderTest.php uses the identical pattern — this brings the new test into alignment with established project conventions.

Fix 2 (reviewer-applied-fix): Changed (string)realpath(...) cast + assertNotEmpty to plain realpath() + assertNotFalse, matching the sibling test's more explicit failure check and removing a silent type coercion.
All 3 tests still pass (10 assertions) after fixes. No regressions.
No blocking architectural or logic issues remain.

comments.note: Added $tempFiles array property and tearDown() method to AbstractLanguageRendererTest. readerFromArray() now appends each temp path to $this->tempFiles, and tearDown() unlinks them. Without this fix, every test run leaked .json files in sys_get_temp_dir(). Pattern mirrors IconBuilderTest.php.

Changed setUp() from `$this->iconsJsonPath = (string)realpath(...)` + `assertNotEmpty(...)` to `$this->iconsJsonPath = realpath(...)` + `assertNotFalse(...)`. The cast silently converted a false return to an empty string; assertNotFalse gives a clearer failure signal and matches the sibling test's convention.

The $iconsJsonPath property is typed `private string` but realpath() returns string|false. Under strict_types=1 this would throw a TypeError if realpath() fails. The assertNotFalse guard in setUp() provides practical safety, and the sibling class uses the same pattern — no change made, but worth noting for a future strict-types audit across test fixtures.

[documentation-forward] The TestableLanguageRenderer class is declared at file scope (outside the test class) due to PHP namespace constraints. A brief inline comment explaining why it lives outside the test class (PHP does not support inner classes) would help future contributors avoid confusion about the structure.
